source_metadata_snapshot.title: Imbalance Price
source_metadata_snapshot.description: This dataset shows all relevant information regarding the imbalance price design. The data is in 15-minute resolution and shows satisfied demand and the imbalance price and contains all the components relevant to the imbalance price, including the aFRR volumes, aFRR volume-weighted average price, and the mFRR marginal price.
source_metadata_snapshot.comment:
**Note**: The data will always reflect the prevailing conditions in the market design. Before March 4th, 2026 the dominating direction was determined by Balancing demand. From March 4th, 2026 the dominating direction is determined by Satisfied demand. Before March 19th, 2025 the imbalance price equal imbalance price from Pricing Module.  

Balancing demand (mFRR SA), can not be found in a new dynamic dataset mFRR Energy Activation Market.

**Find more** information about imbalance price design here: [Slides fra Webinar om nyt ubalancedesign](https://energinet.dk/el/systemydelser/nyheder-om-systemydelser/2025/02/14/slides-fra-webinar-om-nyt-ubalancedesign/) or [Explanatory-note-nyt-design-for-ubalanceafregning.pdf](https://energinet.dk/regler/el/elmarked/)  (Danish) 

---
**API Request Frequency** \
To get the most up-to-date data, calling the API with a dynamic timestamp such as [start=now-PT1H](https://api.energidataservice.dk/dataset/ImbalancePrice?start=now-PT1H) is a good approach. Making a request every 10 minutes or so is sufficient to ensure getting the latest data.
source_metadata_snapshot.author: Energinet

columns.description: A date and time shown in _UTC time zone_. It is the "from" timestamp for the period in which the values are valid. The dataset resolution sets the length of the interval.
columns.comment:
Please note that the _format_ shown in the example applies to data downloaded as JSON or fetched through the API.
The format is slightly different when it is shown on screen or downloaded manually as CSV or XLSX. This is mainly due to readability and consideration for Excel users.

**In preview (in the GUI)** all timestamps are shown as (display convention)
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mmZ
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00Z. 
That is without the seconds. The Z will remind viewers that this is UTC.

In **download (CSV and XLSX)** the date time are exported as
YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm
e.g. 2017-07-14 08:00.
That is without the “T” and the “Z” and the seconds. Excel will recognize it as date-time. The user must remember the convention about time zones.

In **download (JSON and API)** the datetime is exported as
YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ss
e.g. 2017-07-14T08:00:00.
That is without the "Z".

columns.description: Same as bidding zone. Denmark is divided in two price areas (bidding zones) divided by the Great Belt. DK1 is west of the Great Belt and DK2 is east of the Great Belt.
columns.comment: Some datasets contain a limited number of price areas.

columns.description:
The total volume of mFRR activated to cover the balancing need in a bidding zone. Balancing demand show mFRR demand in the bidding zone.
A positive sign indicates mFRR upregulation.
A negative sign indicates mFRR downregulation.
columns.comment: Before March 4th, 2026 This column represented Balancing Demand, hence mFRR demand in the BZ.

columns.description:
Before March 19th, 2025 imbalance price equal imbalance price from pricing module.
Valid from March 19th, 2025: The imbalance price is based on the dominating direction:
Up: max of aFRR component or mFRR price
None: Value of avoided activation, spot price
Down: min of aFRR component or mFRR price
columns.comment: If null, the price is temporarily suspended due to a pricing error. Price will be publish the following working day.

columns.description:
